correctness.rationale: For A=1+y>1, squaring A=(u²+2)/sqrt((u²+2)²−4) gives the unique positive u²=T(y). Constant blending cancels in the fractional levels: δ=fy and w_c²=t_E²[T(cy)−T(y)]. To check the decisive strict inequality, write R−1 as H/J, with H and J the integrals of h=s^(−3/2)(ys+2)^(−3/2) on [a,b] and [b,1]. In H′J−HJ′ the double-integral integrand is h(s)h(t) times 3(t−s)/[(ys+2)(yt+2)], positive almost everywhere. The fixed compact integration intervals allow differentiation and the two limits: normalized kernels tend to s^(−3/2) and s^(−3), giving the claimed L and U. Positive widths fix the sign lost in squaring. The physical restriction is exactly y≥δ, so continuity and strict monotonicity give the unique inverse on [R(δ),U); equality at the lower endpoint is precisely f=1. The upper endpoint is only a limit, with f and u₀ tending to zero at fixed δ. With one positive width, each y≥δ gives a distinct physical fit by rescaling t_E, even at the unblended datum. No exceptional interior a,b or finite y was omitted. Replay: RESULT.md §§1–4 is the all-parameter proof; CHECK.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not run. Their finite decimal checks do not certify uniqueness or numerical stability.

value.rationale: Three simple summary measurements resolve an exact identifiability question for a standard model with severe practical blending degeneracies. The strict feasibility boundary is an independent model-consistency test, the attained boundary distinguishes the unblended case, and the one-width family explains what information a second crossing provides. This is not a noise-stability, measurement sufficiency or survey inference claim.
